new_issues.title: Scoped IBackupService resolved from root service provider
new_issues.evidence_snippet:
var backupService = host.Services.GetRequiredService<IBackupService>();
// IBackupService registered as Scoped in ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:36
new_issues.rule_violated: DI best practice: scoped services should be resolved within a scope, not from root provider
new_issues.remediation: Wrap restore in using (var scope = host.Services.CreateScope()) { var svc = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<IBackupService>(); ... }
new_issues.practical_impact: Works in Blazor WASM due to implicit root scope wrapping, but violates intended lifetime management

new_issues.title: No post-restore database integrity validation
new_issues.evidence_snippet:
await File.WriteAllBytesAsync(_dbPath, data);
// No PRAGMA integrity_check, no SELECT 1 to verify restored file is not corrupt
new_issues.rule_violated: Defensive programming: header magic bytes check doesn't validate internal page consistency
new_issues.remediation: Open a temporary SQLite connection after WriteAllBytesAsync and run PRAGMA integrity_check or SELECT 1

architecture_observations.backup_service_design: Well-designed abstraction with clean interface, schema versioning, proper logging. Only gap is post-restore integrity check.
architecture_observations.startup_flow: Correct ordering: restore -> ensure created -> run. No race conditions or ordering issues.
architecture_observations.accordion_visual_regression: None. accordion-button CSS is pure CSS (::after pseudo-element, .collapsed toggle), no JS required.
architecture_observations.calling_pattern_unchanged: IBackupService abstraction did not change excessive backup invocation pattern — still called on every CRUD mutation.
